digest.component_or_area: Completion verifier banking and verdict assembly
propositions: At search exhaustion, completion verifier incorrectly banks met=false (evidence-of-absence) when the search budget ran out before sufficient evidence could be found, producing false FAIL verdicts on criteria whose evidence exists but was unreached.

The banking WRITE path must distinguish three evidence outcomes (met, refuted, insufficient) by introducing an optional evidence_sufficient:false marker alongside bool met, preserved through harvest-on-overwrite and re-stamped by merge_finalizer_with_bank from the authoritative bank entry.

Genuine refutation (positive evidence of non-completion) remains bare met=false→FAIL, while search-budget exhaustion now banks the marker via CriterionBank.record_insufficient, keeping the model-facing tool bool-only.

All verdict consumers (schema validation, close-gate refusal, rendering paths, sidecar payload) must treat insufficient-evidence FAIL (marker present) differently from unmet-criteria FAIL (marker absent), reporting exhaustion+remediation instead of refutation.
